interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including the preoperative PSA of 5.4 and the surgical pathology revealing a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2). Contributing to risk are the presence of extraprostatic extension and positive surgical margins. Conversely, favorable findings include no seminal vesicle invasion and an absence of lymphovascular invasion. The lack of nodal sampling widens uncertainty regarding nodal status. Biopsy results showed Gleason 3+4 in the right peripheral zone, which aligns with the prostatectomy grade. Prognostic assessment is limited by the missing postoperative PSA data and follow-up information, which would significantly revise risk stratification. Given the current data, a definitive prognosis cannot be established without this subsequent clinical trajectory. The fixed estimated horizon is 62.79 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 37.67–87.91 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including a preoperative PSA of 5.4 and an ISUP grade group 2 pathology from the prostatectomy specimen. Contributing to risk are positive surgical margins and documented extraprostatic extension (pT3a). Countervailing findings include no seminal vesicle invasion and absent lymphovascular invasion. The absence of nodal sampling widens uncertainty regarding nodal status, as pNx is not equivalent to pN0. Biopsy-to-prostatectomy comparison shows concordance in Gleason pattern (3+4/ISUP 2) but the biopsy was limited to the right peripheral zone apex. Prognostic revision would be significantly aided by postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent trajectory over time. The current data is numerically ready, but the lack of previous notes limits comprehensive assessment.
